conversations.segment_role: Establish initial appointments and medical context

dialogue.content: Hey, I need help keeping track of my medical appointments. I've had a rough few months health-wise — stomach issues since February and some sinus stuff too. I had an endoscopy at Zhongshan Hospital on March 20th, Building 2, 4th floor. The results came back showing mild chronic gastritis. Can you help me organize all this?

Of course, I'd be happy to help you organize your medical appointments and health information. It sounds like you've been dealing with quite a bit recently. Let me start noting things down. So far I have: endoscopy at Zhongshan Hospital on March 20th (Building 2, 4th floor), with results showing mild chronic gastritis. That's an important baseline to track. Do you have any follow-up appointments scheduled based on those endoscopy results, or any other visits you'd like me to keep track of?

Dr. Liu told me to come back six weeks after the endoscopy for a follow-up. The endoscopy was March 20th, so the follow-up was originally set for May 1st, a Thursday morning, 9:30 AM, gastroenterology department, Zhongshan Hospital. Dr. Liu Wenjie is the gastroenterologist handling my case. I always try to book morning slots because afternoon waiting rooms are unbearable.

Got it. I've noted your follow-up appointment: May 1st, Thursday, 9:30 AM, with Dr. Liu Wenjie at the gastroenterology department, Zhongshan Hospital. That lines up with the six-week mark after your March 20th endoscopy. I also note your preference for morning appointments — that makes sense since mornings tend to be calmer and less crowded. I'll make sure to flag that preference whenever we discuss scheduling. Do you have any other medical visits or doctors you'd like me to track alongside this?

I also saw Dr. He Mingyu at the ENT department at Zhongshan Hospital on April 8th for sinus congestion. She prescribed a nasal spray and told me to come back if symptoms persist after two weeks. I liked her a lot actually — very efficient, straight to the point, no unnecessary chit-chat. That's exactly the kind of doctor I prefer dealing with.

Noted — Dr. He Mingyu, ENT department, Zhongshan Hospital, visited on April 8th for sinus congestion. She prescribed a nasal spray, and you should return if symptoms persist after two weeks, which would be around April 22nd. I can see you appreciate doctors who are efficient and direct, which is a useful preference to remember. So far your active medical tracking includes the gastroenterology follow-up on May 1st with Dr. Liu and the ENT nasal spray evaluation window. Anything else from the past few months you'd like logged?

My friend Xiao Chen went to Huashan Hospital for a dermatology appointment with a Dr. Zhao in mid-March. She said he was really patient and thorough with explanations. Different style from what I prefer, but she liked it. Also, I used to see a Dr. Tan at Ruijin Hospital for my stomach issues, but I stopped going there last year — no need to track anything about Dr. Tan or Ruijin.

Understood. I'll note Xiao Chen's experience with Dr. Zhao at Huashan Hospital dermatology for reference, but I won't create any active tracking for it since it's her appointment, not yours. And I'll make sure not to include any information about Dr. Tan or Ruijin Hospital in your medical records going forward since that relationship is concluded. Your active medical tracking remains focused on Dr. Liu Wenjie at Zhongshan gastroenterology and Dr. He Mingyu at Zhongshan ENT. Let me know if anything changes with either appointment.

I'll make sure this is prominently noted. Would you like me to set up any kind of reminder framework for the days leading up to April 28th so nothing slips through the cracks?

Yes, that would be great. Also, I realized I've been telling people, including my mom on the phone, that my gastritis diagnosis was moderate. But that's wrong — Dr. Liu was very clear it was mild chronic gastritis. I need to stop misremembering that. The mild part actually matters for treatment decisions, so I want to be precise about it going forward.

That's a really important correction to internalize. Your diagnosis is mild chronic gastritis, not moderate — and you're right that the severity grade matters for treatment planning. Dr. Liu was clear about this after the endoscopy. I'll keep the record accurate: mild chronic gastritis, diagnosed via endoscopy on March 20th at Zhongshan Hospital. It's easy to accidentally upgrade the severity when retelling, especially when you're worried. I'd suggest correcting it with your mom next time you speak so she has accurate information too. The whole period from February through now has been draining. After the endoscopy I was really anxious for several days waiting for results — kept refreshing the hospital app on my phone. I don't handle medical uncertainty well. On a lighter note, the sinus congestion from Dr. He's visit has mostly cleared up with the nasal spray, so at least that's one less thing to worry about.

That's a good idea, let me think about it and get back to you. For now just make sure the April 28th appointment is rock solid in your records. Dr. Liu Wenjie, gastroenterology, Zhongshan Hospital, Monday 9:30 AM. I really can't afford to miss it or get confused about the date again.

Since you have the 9:30 AM slot, you'll be at your sharpest, which aligns with your preference for morning visits. Confirmed and locked in: April 28th, Monday, 9:30 AM, Dr. Liu Wenjie, gastroenterology department, Zhongshan Hospital. This is your top-priority appointment and I have it clearly recorded. answer.question: If someone reviewed our entire conversation history about my gastroenterology follow-up date, what would they see as the full sequence of scheduling changes — which dates were actually adopted each time, which one was only floated but never went through, and what's the final plan?
answer.expected_answer: The sequence was: (1) May 1st, Thursday, 9:30 AM — the original date set six weeks after the March 20th endoscopy; (2) April 28th, Monday, 9:30 AM — rescheduled due to a work trip, replacing May 1st; (3) April 30th, Wednesday, 9:30 AM — floated because of a mandatory team meeting conflict, but never actually booked with the hospital; (4) April 28th, Monday, 9:30 AM — reconfirmed after the team meeting moved to the afternoon. The final plan is April 28th, Monday, 9:30 AM, Dr. Liu Wenjie, gastroenterology, Zhongshan Hospital.
answer.gold_memory_state: Chain: May 1st (confirmed, superseded) → April 28th (confirmed, active) → April 30th (tentative, never adopted) → April 28th (reconfirmed, final). Final state: April 28th, Monday, 9:30 AM, Dr. Liu Wenjie, gastroenterology, Zhongshan Hospital.

must_not_include: April 30th described as confirmed or adopted
harmful_extra: omitting April 30th from the sequence entirely
claiming April 30th was the final date
adding dates not discussed
harmless_extra: mentioning the work trip reason for first reschedule
mentioning the team meeting reason for the tentative change

diagnostic_checks.stale_value: Fails if the model treats April 30th or May 1st as the final adopted date.
diagnostic_checks.trajectory_order: Fails if the model misordering the sequence (e.g., placing April 30th after the final reconfirmation, or placing May 1st after April 28th in the chain).
diagnostic_checks.final_state: Fails if the model does not identify April 28th, Monday, 9:30 AM as the final confirmed state.
diagnostic_checks.intermediate_state: Fails if the model does not correctly identify April 30th as a tentative intermediate state that was never adopted.
diagnostic_checks.trajectory_provenance: Fails if the model cannot attribute the changes to the correct reasons (work trip for first reschedule, team meeting for tentative shift, meeting moved for reversion).

gold_reasoning_chain: Step 1: Original appointment set for May 1st, Thursday, 9:30 AM — six weeks after the March 20th endoscopy. Status: confirmed.
Step 2: Rescheduled to April 28th, Monday, 9:30 AM due to a work trip. May 1st superseded. Status: confirmed.
Step 3: April 30th, Wednesday, 9:30 AM floated due to a mandatory team meeting on April 28th morning. The user had not yet called the hospital. Status: tentative, never adopted.
Step 4: Team meeting moved to the afternoon, clearing April 28th morning. User reconfirmed April 28th, Monday, 9:30 AM. April 30th discarded. Status: confirmed, final.
Inference: The full trajectory is May 1st → April 28th → April 30th (tentative only) → April 28th (reconfirmed). Final state is April 28th, Monday, 9:30 AM.

gold_provenance.quote: the follow-up was originally set for May 1st, a Thursday morning, 9:30 AM, gastroenterology department, Zhongshan Hospital
I had to reschedule the May 1st follow-up with Dr. Liu because of a work trip. I moved it to April 28th, Monday, 9:30 AM, same department and hospital.
My manager just told me there's a mandatory team meeting on April 28th morning. I'll probably have to push the follow-up to April 30th, Wednesday, same 9:30 AM slot with Dr. Liu.

Good news — the team meeting got moved to the afternoon, so April 28th morning is clear again. I'm keeping the follow-up on April 28th, Monday, 9:30 AM with Dr. Liu at Zhongshan Hospital gastroenterology.
